name: Ralte
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Otsuka, Kosei 2021. ラルテー語の音韻とクキ・チン祖語 [A phonological comparison of Ralte and Proto-Kuki-Chin]. ありあけ 熊本大学言語学論集 (ARIAKE Kumamoto University Linguistic Papers) 20: 21-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Revised phonology (sec. 2, pp. 22-25): syllable (C1)V(C2)(C3)/T, three tones (low level, rising, falling) plus a possible 4th pitch pattern on glottal/short checked syllables; sec. 2.3 p. 24: long vowels/diphthongs shorten in the first syllable of compounds and derived words and that syllable surfaces with low level tone. No 強勢/ストレス/アクセント anywhere in the text.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.6 音韻 (pp. 164-165): syllable (C1)V(C2)(C3)/T, consonants, vowels, 2.6.4 three tonemes (rising, low level, falling); short open syllables all low level; checked syllables low pitch / high after low. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Otsuka, Kosei 2015. ラルテー語における音韻体系: ミゾ語およびティディム・チン語との対照的考察 [The phonological system of the Ralte language: a comparative study of Ralte, Mizo, and Tiddim Chin]. 東京大学言語学論集 (TULIP) 36: e49-e59.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Body is a scanned image (read visually, all 11 pp.). Sec. 2.1 syllable C1(V1)V2(V3)(C2)/T; 2.2 consonants; 2.3 vowels i e a o u with length contrast; 2.4 tone: three tonemes (rising LH, low level LL, falling HL), checked syllables low pitch (high after low-level tone). No mention of stress/accent (強勢/アクセント).

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1904. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III Tibeto-Burman Family, Part III Specimens of the Kuki-Chin and Burma Groups. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Ralte' pp. 75-78 (+ specimen).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on accent/stress. 'Pronunciation' paragraph (p. 75-76) only discusses vowel length ('probably every final vowel of a word or syllable is long, just as in Lushei'), h for abrupt shortening, euphonic v/m, ch ~ Lushei f; based solely on a Prodigal Son specimen.
